payload.description:
## Trigger

When a consumer repo installs basicly, I want it to receive one reviewed `.claude/settings.json` baseline, and basicly to dogfood the same file, so every repo gets the same permission and config posture instead of a hand-copied variant that drifts.

## Context

`basicly permissions-build` and `hooks-build` already co-own four parts of `.claude/settings.json` (`src/basicly/claude_settings.py`): the managed `permissions.deny` list from `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml`, the managed agent hooks, `worktree.bgIsolation`, and `subagentPromptCacheTtl`. Everything else is hand-authored per repo. A review of the settings files across the housed repos of one workspace on 2026-09-25 found:

- basicly and one consumer (terminal) carry a hand-copied blanket `permissions.allow` of `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`. In default or acceptEdits mode that runs every shell command unprompted, so the prefix-anchored deny list is the only check (see basicly-ejowvgn, basicly-tcmy.40). In auto mode the classifier still reviewed a Bash call in a repo with that allow, so the entry adds no value there.
- The consumers drifted: terminal adds `ask: ["Bash(git push *)"]` and denies `git rebase*`. basicly does not.
- basicly and terminal set `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, which is deprecated in favour of `attribution`.
- In one consumer (burndown-chart) a blanket `*.json` rule in `.gitignore` ignores `.claude/settings.json`, so its projected hooks and deny list are not versioned. `permissions-check` and `hooks-check` pass locally and say nothing.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` in basicly and terminal has accumulated one-off allows with absolute scratchpad and worktree paths, plus broad entries (`Bash(git *)`, `Bash(uv run *)`, `Bash(python3 -)`).
- Auto mode trust (`autoMode.environment`) lives in user settings. The one shipped by hand names only basicly as trusted, has no `$defaults` entry in `environment`, and makes every other repo of the same owner look external.

## Proposed baseline (projected, co-owned keys only)

- `permissions.deny`: unchanged source (`permissions.yaml`), plus the entries from basicly-tcmy.40.
- `permissions.ask`: a new managed list, first entry `Bash(git push*)`, sourced from the same catalog file as deny.
- `permissions.allow`: basicly projects no blanket tool allow. It either projects nothing, or a small scoped list of read-only commands. The existing blanket entries are removed from basicly's own file.
- `attribution` replaces `includeCoAuthoredBy`, keeping the object form so older clients still load the file.
- Existing co-owned keys stay: hooks, `worktree.bgIsolation`, `subagentPromptCacheTtl`.
- `permissions-check` refuses when `git check-ignore .claude/settings.json` matches, and names the ignore rule and the negation line that fixes it.
- Auto mode: optional, opt-in `--user` step (like `install_hook.py --user`). It prints or merges an `autoMode` block that keeps `$defaults` in every section and trusts the repo's forge owner, not one repo. Verify first which settings sources Claude Code reads `autoMode` from (interface-facts); do not project it into project settings if Claude Code ignores it there.

## Out of scope

`settings.local.json` stays user-owned. A lint that only warns on absolute paths or broad allows there is a possible follow-up.
payload.requirements:
- The ask list and the deny list stay in one catalog file. The projection reads that file and never copies it.
- Keys a consumer authored by hand outside the managed set stay untouched; the merge is additive, like `merge_permission_deny`.
- Commit no machine path, user name or host name into the projected file.
payload.title: Ship one reviewed Claude settings.json baseline to consumers and dogfood it

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a person runs Claude Code in auto mode in a repository that basicly installed, I want the shipped permission rules to work in that mode, so I can work without prompts for routine read and check commands.

## Context

Request from terminal's owner, 2026-09-25, checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes and /auto-mode-config the same day. Today .claude/settings.json ships a blanket Bash, Edit and Write allow plus 25 deny rules, and only the deny list is projected. In auto mode, broad rules that grant arbitrary code execution are dropped: blanket Bash(*), wildcarded interpreters, package-manager run commands, Agent and Monitor rules. Narrow rules stay and resolve before the classifier. An ask rule always prompts. Project settings cannot carry autoMode, so the trust context lives only in ~/.claude/settings.json or managed settings. /auto-mode-setup writes autoMode.environment without $defaults by design, and on this machine that list names basicly as the only trusted repo; after 3 blocks in a row or 20 in total, auto mode pauses. Proposals: (a) project the whole permissions block with narrow allows and no blanket Bash; (b) a user-level check of autoMode.environment; (c) not a basicly defect.
payload.requirements: Every shipped rule has an effect in the mode it is meant for.
payload.title: fit the shipped permissions to auto mode

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When install runs over an existing `.claude/settings.json` with uncommitted or untracked content, a `.basicly-bak` copy equal to the old bytes exists afterwards, and install prints its path.
- When the file is malformed JSON, install exits non-zero, names the file and the parse position, and writes nothing.
- When the file carries a user-authored key, a user hook and `includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, afterwards the key and hook are unchanged, `attribution` holds the equivalent value, and `includeCoAuthoredBy` is gone.
- When `settings.local.json` carries an absolute path or a blanket allow, install lists the finding and the file's bytes are unchanged.
- When `--dry-run` runs, it prints the key-level summary and no file changes.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When `basicly install` runs in a repo that already has `.claude/settings.json` (or `settings.local.json`), I want to merge the baseline into it by a written rule and keep a restorable copy of the old file, so I can install into an existing repo without losing or silently changing its settings.

## Context

Today `permissions-build` and `hooks-build` merge additively into `.claude/settings.json` (`merge_permission_deny`, `merge_agent_hooks` in `src/basicly/claude_settings.py`) and keep no copy. The `.basicly-bak` backups cover scaffold files and untracked projected files only (`cli.py` `SCAFFOLD_BACKUP_SUFFIX`, `projection.back_up_unrecognised`). A malformed settings file is not refused by name: probed 2026-09-25 in a scratch repo, `sync_permission_deny` raises `JSONDecodeError` on a trailing comma, and `cmd_permissions_build` has no handler for it.

## Merge rule, per key

- Managed lists (`permissions.deny`, `permissions.ask`): union, existing entries kept, order kept.
- Managed hooks: replaced by script identity, as today; a user hook on the same event stays.
- `permissions.allow`: kept. Install reports an entry that makes a managed rule moot (a blanket `Bash`, `Edit` or `Write`; an allow that equals a managed `ask` entry) and does not delete it.
- Deprecated keys (`includeCoAuthoredBy`): migrated to `attribution` with the same meaning, and the old key removed.
- Any key basicly does not own: left byte-for-byte as it was.
- `settings.local.json`: never written. Install lists findings only: absolute paths, user or host names, broad allows (`Bash(git *)`, `Bash(uv run *)`, `Bash(python3 -)`), and allows that override a managed `ask`.

## Backup

Before the first write that changes an existing `.claude/settings.json`, install writes `.claude/settings.json.basicly-bak`, unless the file is tracked and has no uncommitted change (git holds that copy). Install prints the backup path and a key-level summary of what changed. `--dry-run` prints the same summary and writes nothing.
payload.requirements:
- One merge function owns the rule. `permissions-build`, `hooks-build` and install call it; none copies it.
- A regression test covers each per-key rule and the malformed-file refusal.
payload.title: Merge the baseline into an existing Claude settings file by rule and keep a restorable copy

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When an agent follows the prompt in a repo with an existing settings file, it produces the classification table and the diff before any write.
- When the plan would remove or narrow a user entry or edit `.gitignore`, the agent stops for approval and changes nothing without it.
- When `basicly install --dry-run --json` runs, it prints a per-file, per-key plan that a JSON parser reads.
- When the install finishes, the agent reports `permissions-check` and `hooks-check` results and the backup path.
payload.description:
## Trigger

When a coding agent installs basicly into a repo, I want it to analyse the repo's existing agent settings before it merges anything, so I can get a merge fitted to what the repo already relies on, and not a mechanical union the agent cannot explain.

## Context

basicly has an agent install prompt for the tracker package only (`packages/basicly-tracker/README.md#install-with-a-coding-agent`, linked from README.md). Nothing guides an agent through installing basicly itself. The mechanical rule in basicly-f002zye cannot judge intent: whether a blanket allow is deliberate, whether a hand-added `ask` or deny (for example terminal's `git rebase*` deny) should stay, or whether `settings.local.json` entries are stale.

## Shape

- An agent install prompt (README section plus a skill) that runs, in order:
  1. `basicly install --dry-run --json`: a machine-readable plan per file and key, so the agent does not parse prose. This needs the `--json` form.
  2. Read `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, the `.gitignore` rules for both, and the user-level `autoMode` block (read only).
  3. Classify every existing entry: kept as is, superseded by a managed entry, conflicts with a managed entry, risky (blanket allow, interpreter allow, absolute path), or stale (points at a path that no longer exists).
  4. Show the user one table of the entries it plans to change and why, with the proposed merged file as a diff. Wait for approval before it removes or narrows any user entry, or edits an ignore file.
  5. Run `basicly install`, then `permissions-check` and `hooks-check`, and report the backup path from basicly-f002zye.
- The agent never edits user-level settings. For auto mode it prints the proposed `autoMode` block (with `$defaults`) for the user to apply. The classifier refuses that edit as self-modification (observed 2026-09-25).
payload.requirements:
- The classification uses the same merge rule as basicly-f002zye. The prompt reads the `--json` plan; it does not restate the rule.
- Validate it as a consumer: a scratch repo seeded with the settings shapes from the parent record (blanket allow, ignored settings file, stale local allows).
payload.title: Guide an agent-driven install to analyse existing Claude settings before merging
